issues.description: Missing input validation on subscription upgrade endpoint. The userId, plan, and addons parameters are passed directly to upgradeSubscription() without validation, creating potential for injection attacks, type confusion, or privilege escalation.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive input validation for userId (ensure it's a valid number/string), plan (whitelist allowed plans), and addons (validate structure and allowed values).

issues.description: No authentication or authorization on sensitive subscription upgrade endpoint. Any user can potentially upgrade any userId to any plan without authentication checks.
issues.suggestion: Implement authentication middleware to verify the requesting user's identity and authorization to perform subscription upgrades.

issues.description: Missing security headers and middleware. No helmet.js or CORS configuration, leaving the application vulnerable to common web attacks (XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, etc.).
issues.suggestion: Add security middleware like helmet.js and configure CORS properly.

issues.description: No request rate limiting configured. The application is vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks and brute-force attempts, especially on the subscription upgrade endpoint.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting using express-rate-limit.

issues.description: Missing error handling middleware. Unhandled errors in async operations or middleware will crash the server or leak error details to clients.
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive error handling middleware at the end of the middleware chain.

issues.description: Integer ID conversion without validation. Number(req.params.id) can return NaN for invalid input, potentially causing unexpected behavior in toggleTodo/removeTodo functions.
issues.suggestion: Validate the ID parameter before conversion using parseInt with validation.

issues.description: No request body size limit configured. The express.json() middleware has no size limit, making the server vulnerable to payload-based DoS attacks.
issues.suggestion: Set a reasonable body size limit: app.use(express.json({ limit: '10kb' }));

issues.description: Inconsistent error response format. Some endpoints return { error: '...' } while the structure varies. This makes client-side error handling more difficult.
issues.suggestion: Standardize error responses across all endpoints using a helper function.

issues.description: Route handlers are inline anonymous functions, making the code harder to test and maintain. Business logic is mixed with routing concerns.
issues.suggestion: Extract route handlers into separate controller functions for better testability and maintainability.

issues.description: Server startup logic mixed with route definitions. This makes it harder to use the app instance in tests without starting the server.
issues.suggestion: Separate server startup into a dedicated file (e.g., server.js vs app.js).

issues.description: Duplicated error handling logic for 404 responses across multiple endpoints. The pattern 'if (!todo) return res.status(404)...' is repeated.
issues.suggestion: Create a reusable helper function for 404 handling.

issues.description: Console.log used for application logging. In production, structured logging with proper log levels is essential for debugging and monitoring.
issues.suggestion: Use a proper logging library like winston or pino.

issues.description: HTTP 200 returned for subscription upgrade instead of 201 (Created) or 204 (No Content). While not incorrect, using 201 for resource creation or modification is more semantically accurate.
issues.suggestion: Use appropriate HTTP status codes: res.status(201).json(...);

codeQuality.summary: The server.js file contains several critical security vulnerabilities that must be addressed immediately. The most severe issues are: (1) No authentication/authorization on the subscription upgrade endpoint, allowing any user to upgrade any account; (2) Complete lack of input validation on the subscription endpoint parameters; (3) Missing essential security middleware (helmet, CORS, rate limiting). Additionally, there are high-severity concerns around error handling, request body size limits, and ID parameter validation. From a maintainability perspective, the code mixes routing with business logic, uses inline handlers that are difficult to test, and lacks proper error handling middleware. The code quality score of 42/100 reflects these critical security gaps and architectural concerns.

testCoverage.summary: CRITICAL COVERAGE GAP: src/server.js has ZERO test coverage. No test files exist for this Express application server, leaving all 5 API endpoints and multiple code branches completely untested. The file contains 15+ distinct testable paths including 5 HTTP endpoints, 4 error-handling branches, 3 edge cases, and 1 new premium subscription feature (PR-3). HIGH-PRIORITY GAPS: POST /subscriptions/upgrade endpoint (business-critical monetization), POST /todos validation (input validation failures), all 404 error paths, and core CRUD operations lack verification. The estimated coverage is 0% because no tests exist. A comprehensive test suite should aim for 90%+ coverage including all success paths, error paths, and edge cases.

refactorings.summary: The server.js file is functional but has several structural opportunities for improvement. The highest-impact refactorings are: (1) extracting route handlers into separate modules using Express Router pattern to improve organization and testability, (2) adding input validation to the subscription endpoint for consistency and security, and (3) extracting the server initialization to eliminate side effects on module import. Medium-impact improvements include creating reusable middleware for ID parsing and error responses, and modernizing to async/await for future flexibility. Overall, the code would benefit from better separation of concerns and more consistent patterns across all endpoints.

codeQuality.summary: The code has significant maintainability and best-practice issues. PRIMARY CONCERNS: (1) Extensive use of loose equality (==) instead of strict equality (===) throughout - a common source of bugs in JavaScript. (2) Heavy code duplication in addon pricing logic with identical amounts repeated across all plan tiers. (3) Magic numbers scattered throughout without constants - pricing values should be centralized. (4) Missing input validation on all parameters, allowing invalid data to flow through. MODERATE ISSUES: Repetitive if-else chains that should use object lookups; lack of documentation; silent failure on invalid plans returns 0 instead of throwing errors. The code uses some modern features like optional chaining but needs refactoring to use configuration objects for pricing, implement proper validation, switch to strict equality, and eliminate duplication.

testCoverage.summary: The src/subscription.js file has ZERO test coverage - no test files exist for this module. The file exports two functions: calculatePrice (38 lines with multiple conditional branches) and upgradeSubscription (9 lines). calculatePrice contains 3 plan branches (basic/pro/enterprise), an else branch for invalid plans, and 2 addon branches each with 3 nested plan conditionals. This creates at least 15+ distinct code paths that are completely untested. The upgradeSubscription function integrates with calculatePrice and adds timestamp generation. Critical untested scenarios include: invalid plan handling (returns 0 silently), null/undefined addon handling, multi-addon combinations, and timestamp generation. Given the financial nature of subscription pricing, the lack of tests poses significant risk for billing errors.

refactorings.summary: Found 7 refactoring opportunities with 3 high-impact improvements. The most critical refactoring is replacing the nested if-else chains with declarative configuration objects (PLAN_PRICES and ADDON_PRICES), which would reduce the calculatePrice function from 35 lines to 8 lines and eliminate 12 conditional branches. The current implementation has significant duplication: each addon adds the same price regardless of plan type, yet requires 6 redundant conditionals. Modern JavaScript patterns (const, optional chaining, object lookup, reduce) would make this code more maintainable, testable, and extensible. Overall impact: reduces cyclomatic complexity from 13 to 1, eliminates 30+ lines of code, and makes pricing configuration data-driven rather than procedural.

recommendations.description: The subscription upgrade endpoint has no authentication or authorization checks, allowing any user to potentially upgrade any userId to any plan. This is a severe security vulnerability that could lead to unauthorized access and financial loss.

Missing input validation on the subscription upgrade endpoint parameters (userId, plan, addons). This creates potential for injection attacks, type confusion, or privilege escalation. Both server.js and subscription.js lack proper parameter validation.

Both files have 0% test coverage with no test files existing. This is especially critical for the subscription pricing logic which handles financial calculations. Billing errors could directly impact revenue and customer trust.

Missing essential security middleware including helmet.js (for security headers), CORS configuration, and rate limiting. The application is vulnerable to XSS, clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and DoS attacks.

Heavy code duplication and use of anti-patterns. The subscription.js file uses loose equality (==) instead of strict equality (===), has magic numbers scattered throughout, and contains 18 lines of redundant conditionals in addon pricing logic.
Missing global error handling middleware in server.js. Unhandled errors will crash the server or leak error details to clients. Additionally, error responses are inconsistent across endpoints.

Route handlers are inline anonymous functions mixing business logic with routing concerns. Extract into separate controller modules using Express Router pattern for better testability and maintainability.
Pricing values are hardcoded as magic numbers throughout subscription.js. Extract into a centralized configuration object (PLAN_PRICES, ADDON_PRICES) to make updates safer and enable dynamic pricing.

The calculatePrice function has 15+ distinct code paths (plan tiers, addon combinations, edge cases) that are completely untested. Add comprehensive unit tests covering all branches, especially invalid plan handling which currently returns $0 silently.
Server startup logic is mixed with route definitions, making it difficult to test the app without starting the server. Separate into app.js (configuration) and server.js (startup) files.
